defect_interactions.interaction_type: FCC twins within the FCC Cu-rich particles
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: SAED patterns show the fine interface particles have an FCC crystalline structure with FCC twins frequently observed within the particles; the Cu-rich particles are rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn and slightly poor in Al, while the β-Mn is poor in Cu.

interfaces.interface_notes: For the 19Al alloy aged at ≥600 °C the α matrix is almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging and numerous fine precipitates are distributed within the β-Mn; the volume fraction of these FCC Cu-rich + BCC precipitates between the β-Mn interfaces increases with Al content, which lowers the absolute volume fraction of β-Mn and the overall hardness. The FCC Cu-rich phase is the more ductile constituent (the BCC phase is harder), so the decrease of the ductile FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces with increasing Al content lowers the fracture toughness.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with the nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) were produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching; this is the common baseline state (263.8 ± 1.1 HV for the 19Al alloy).

Solution-treated 19Al samples aged at 650 °C for 10 h, followed by water quenching. Aging temperature (not time) dominates the hardness of the 19Al alloy; the 650 °C series is essentially time-independent at ~801–811 HV.

hardness.region: bulk (19Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester using a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported; samples aged at 650 °C for 10 h then water quenched.

structures.overall_structure: Solution-treated (1100 °C/10 min + oil quench) 19Al alloy consists of a single α (BCC) phase; the 19Al IPF map shows a much finer, equiaxed, multi-coloured grain structure than the 15Al/17Al alloys, and no γ (FCC) region is resolved in the phase map.

phases_present.morphology: near fully transformed matrix of near-equiaxed grains
fine dispersed particles within the β-Mn
fine particles situated at the interfaces between the β-Mn

precipitates.distribution: at the interfaces between the β-Mn

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 650 °C for 10 h the α matrix of the 19Al alloy has almost completely transformed into β-Mn; numerous fine precipitates (new BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase) are present within the β-Mn / at the β-Mn interfaces. The 650 °C series of the 19Al alloy is essentially time-independent at ~801–811 HV (811.2 ± 19.5 HV at 10 h), with the 625–650 °C series plateauing near 800–860 HV.
